calls.head: Strength vs. Strength
calls.body: The Blues are the league’s best for chance quality, but the Predators are near the top at preventing dangerous shots. Our lean: the Blues’ chance quality wins out.
calls.call: The Blues’ chances are more dangerous than the league average (a 6.3% chance of scoring on the average shot) against the Predators.
calls.nums: St. Louis 1st for chance quality (a 7.1% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Nashville 8th for preventing dangerous shots

chips.tip: St. Louis: a 7.1% chance of scoring on the average shot, 1st of 32. Playing style, this season blended with last, 7 and 7 games this season.
Nashville: a 6.1% chance of scoring on the average shot against, 8th of 32. Playing style, this season blended with last, 7 and 7 games this season.

calls.happened: On chance quality, St. Louis had 5.4% a shot. The league average is 6.3% a shot, and they came in at 7.1% a shot.

lane.tip: St. Louis tonight (the filled dot) against the league average (the tick). The call needed the dot above the average. The ring is where they usually sit.

calls.title: Nashville won the standoff
calls.plain: The Predators kept the Blues under the league average on chance quality.
calls.said: the Blues’ shooters would win the standoff with the Predators’ defense

calls.head: Top line on top line: O'Reilly vs. Thomas
calls.body: At home, the Predators keep sending O'Reilly’s line (Stamkos, O'Reilly and Kerfoot) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Andrew Brunette has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Blues’ first line is Holloway, Thomas and Snuggerud.
calls.call: The Predators’ L1 (Stamkos, O'Reilly and Kerfoot) spends at least 53% of its 5-on-5 time against the Blues’ first line, against about 34% with no line matching.
calls.nums: At home: 72% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 34% with no line matching
calls.cite: Matchups · Nashville home games this season · 4 games, 41 minutes for this group at 5-on-5

With no line matching, this group would face first lines about 34% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

calls.happened: Nashville broke up that line tonight: Stamkos, O'Reilly, Kerfoot were together for only 2:06 at 5-on-5, so the matchup this call described never really happened.
calls.said: Andrew Brunette would send Stamkos, O'Reilly and Kerfoot out against the Blues’ first line again

calls.head: The Blues should drive the play
calls.body: At 5-on-5, the Blues have been near the top of the league at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Predators near the bottom. The ice should tilt the Blues’ way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.
calls.call: The Blues get the bigger share of the 5-on-5 chances.

NSH.head: We had Nashville as slight underdogs (43%), and they pulled it off.

STL.head: We leaned St. Louis’s way (57%), but Nashville had other ideas.

surprises.head: Nashville found the good looks for once
surprises.body: Nashville usually gets some of the league’s least dangerous shots, and St. Louis is one of the league’s best at preventing dangerous shots. Not tonight: Nashville’s shots at 5-on-5 had an 8.3% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 5.8% (about 5.4% against St. Louis) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 35 games.

story.head: Wilsby has three assists as the Predators beat the Blues
paras: Philip Broberg got the scoring started for the Blues early in the first. Jonathan Marchessault tied it up for Nashville on a penalty shot a little over two minutes later. Filip Forsberg put the Predators up 2-1 less than four minutes later, and Adam Edström made it 3-1 shorthanded early in the second. Jimmy Snuggerud cut Nashville’s lead to 3-2 on the power play 31 seconds later, but that was as close as they got. Ryan O'Reilly stretched the lead to 4-2 early in the third, and Jack Drury scored his first goal for Nashville midway through the period to make it 5-2. Adam Wilsby finished with three assists.

The Predators drove the play, and the scoreboard caught up. Juuse Saros made 24 saves for the Predators, and Jordan Binnington allowed five goals on 24 shots. The Preds moved to 3-2-3 and climbed to sixth in the Central, while the Blues fell to 3-4-1, slipping to seventh in the Central.

items.text: The Predators won for the first time in four games.
Justin Barron played his first game back in Nashville.
Mason McTavish has a point in six straight games.
Filip Forsberg scored again against St. Louis, and has twelve goals in twelve games against them since 2023-24.
